title: Forge seat record v8
description: v7 with two members opened, and nothing else (decision 0075 ruling 2, and its addendum of 2026-11-21 for root_session.kind, amending decision 0056 ruling 3's closed kind). transcript.kind and root_session.kind are each one lowercase word of letters, digits and single inner hyphens, at most 40 characters, declared by the harness's adapter rather than listed here: the schema admits the grammar, and the engine's writer refuses, at append, a kind no loaded adapter declares. Readers judge a record by this schema alone, so an exported journal verifies without the adapters that wrote it. none keeps its meaning for a transcript, whose locator and home are then empty, and is refused as a root session kind: a root session is a confirmed provider session or it is absent. Every v7 kind fits the grammar and no other member changes, so every valid v7 record is a valid v8 record. v7 is not edited; this is a new file beside it, and the 0.14 line and later read v8. v7's description follows. v6's vocabulary (decisions 0034, 0035, 0042, 0046, 0056 and 0065) plus decision 0109 ruling 1's gate report: a successful result may carry findings, follow_ups and covered, and in the protected phase the engine-written checked_head its effect's check accepted (ruling 7), beside result, inputs, notes, state and the accounting fields. v6 is not edited; this is a new file beside it, and a record is validated against the version its run's engine wrote (the 0.14 line and later read v7, the 0.12 and 0.13 lines read v6). The definitions are v6's, kept under $defs, with four more: one finding, one covered record, and the digest and path they name. findings is the seat's report with the site the engine stamped on each entry (ruling 3): a stable id matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ of at most 64 bytes, the 64-hex site digest of the compiled site that reported it, a repository-relative file, an optional positive line, a non-empty summary, a severity in the closed none < info < low < medium < high < critical vocabulary and a security flag. The key is (site, id); file, line, summary, severity and security are the record, not the identity. follow_ups has the same shape and is engine-written. covered is engine-written and tagged by kind (ruling 7): head with exactly one of head (the commit the gate read) or head_digest (the SHA-256 of the protected phase's decide-time head string), beside dirty, and no base; or artifacts with each declared file's repository-relative path and SHA-256. Every added property is optional and nothing v6 admitted is taken away, so every valid v6 record is a valid v7 record and is never rewritten or back-filled, while a v6 record carrying any of them is refused under v6. A seat that writes covered, follow_ups, checked_head or a finding's site is refused by the engine's result admission before this contract is asked; this contract checks only the shape.

model.description: The harness-reported served model, never a configured pin. The only non-provider values are the two sentinels ruled by decision 0031. It is the provider's claim, not proof (decision 0035 ruling 2): no harness discloses quantization, hardware routing, or a substitution made at peak load, and the same string comes back whichever happened.

effort.description: The effort configured for the model, as the harness echoes it back (decision 0035 ruling 3). CONFIGURATION, never a report: no harness discloses a served effort, so this is the setting that applied after every profile and plugin layer — read from the harness's own echo, never from the bundle's pin, and never presented as a measurement of what the model did. A harness whose lanes carry a real effort control but echo no value writes decision 0031's 'not reported'; a driver with no model turn writes 'not applicable'. The two sentinels are reused rather than reinvented, and the distinction between them is load-bearing: a control that exists but goes unreported is not a control that does not exist.

boundary.description: Which boundary stood at this seat's site (decision 0046 ruling 3): one of the five words of decision 0046 ruling 1, or decision 0031's sentinel not applicable for a site without hands. Stamped by the engine, the only party that knows which boundary it built; a driver's value never survives the stamp. v5 changes nothing about it.

root_session.description: The provider-confirmed root session this launch stands on (proposed decision 0056 ruling 3). Constructed only after measured provider evidence confirms the exact root opened; a resume flag, a preassigned creation id, an argv echo or an exit status of zero is not confirmation. Distinct from transcript, which is decision 0032's retained locator: a storage directory is not a provider handle.

kind.description: Which provider's session this is, as the harness's adapter declares it (decision 0075 ruling 2; its addendum of 2026-11-21 opens this member). LaneTally retains claude's kind, because its wrapper wraps that harness. none is not a root session kind: a root session is confirmed or absent.

id.description: The COMPLETE provider identifier, never truncated to fit. Each provider's own grammar is narrower than this bound; an identifier that cannot fit losslessly is not recorded and not offered.

harness_version.description: The version of the CLI or wrapper OBSERVED at the invocation that opened this root, read through that harness's measured version interface. Never the version the declaration wished for: a later invocation compares what it observes against this, and a change disables resume rather than assuming the interface held.

wrapper_digest.description: The measured digest of a wrapper's own identity where one stands between the engine and the harness. Absent for plain claude, codex and dsh.

persistent.description: Whether this root persists after the invocation ends, from the established semantics of the shape that opened it. A root that does not persist establishes the site's newest owner and can never be offered.

transcript.description: Decision 0032's retained, harness-owned locator. It carries an id or path and never transcript content.

kind.description: Which harness's transcript this locates, as the harness's adapter declares it (decision 0075 ruling 2), or none, whose locator and home are empty.

input_tokens.description: All reported input tokens, inclusive of cache_read_tokens.

output_tokens.description: All reported output tokens, inclusive of reasoning_output_tokens.

cache_read_tokens.description: The cache-read subset of input_tokens; never a second addend.

cache_write_tokens.description: Tokens the harness reports as written to or created in its cache.

reasoning_output_tokens.description: The reasoning subset of output_tokens, in the way cache_read_tokens is a subset of input_tokens; never a second addend. The three harnesses report it at different granularities and this field admits all three without inventing the others. Where a harness reports no figure for this record the field is ABSENT — never zero, and never back-filled from a run total.

tool.description: A bounded harness tool identifier, never its arguments or command.

target.description: A bounded file-path-only target for the tool call; never a command, URL, tool argument object, or prose.

site_ref.description: The engine's structural site stamp (proposed decision 0056 ruling 1): the digest of this invocation's run-scoped site path — outer seat, selected case, body kind and full member/step path. Stamped by the engine exactly as boundary is; a driver's value never survives the stamp. Its presence is what tells a reader that the row was written by an engine enacting 0056, which is why the two conditions below are scoped on it.

instance_ref.description: The engine's owner stamp (proposed decision 0056 ruling 2): the digest of the adapter instance that ran this site — agent, provider, model, effort, chain index, driver identity, command template, adapter declaration, engine version, pinned bundle, class, boundary and hands declaration. Carries no resolved credential, provider-home content or private argv.

tool.description: The actual concrete tool, in v5's vocabulary. 256 bytes on an attributed checkpoint; the last condition below holds every other row to v5's 80.

capability.description: The abstract capability the call was made through, from the attempt's selected sealed holding; never a name inferred from the tool.

dialect.description: The tool dialect that served the capability at this site.

call_id.description: The engine-owned, nonsecret identity of one call within its attempt: a native call's attempt plus measured harness call identifier, or a broker call's attempt, broker and sequence. Never model content.

call_state.description: observed for a native call the harness reported, which claims no completion; succeeded, failed, refused or interrupted for a settled broker call. started is a private ledger record, never a public checkpoint, and is not a member.

response_sha256.description: The sha256 of a retained response artifact the engine published, beside succeeded or failed only.

resume_refusal.description: Why an offer that was made could not be taken. v4's five tokens name a bad identifier, a missing or unsupported codex sandbox class, an argv that cannot travel and a harness that rejected the handle. v5 adds five more: unsupported-resume for a shape whose adapter declares no safe resume interface, unverified-harness for a CLI or wrapper identity that is missing, changed or unreadable, restrictions-unavailable for a shape whose current restrictions cannot be re-imposed on a rejoin, instance-changed for a detectable owner or client drift, and nonpersistent-session for a root the shape does not persist.

authored.description: The engine's authorship of a record it writes beside a verdict, a sequence step's finish or a panel member's (fix round 0109a1r4): engine-written, and a driver's live checkpoint that carries it, or names either marker's step, is refused, so a reader admits a checkpoint as a verdict by this field and never by its step word. No earlier version admits it, so no record a v6-era engine wrote carries it.

result.description: A sequence step's result, journaled with its checkpoint. An object, as v6 admits it, on every row a v6-era engine wrote; on a row the engine authored (authored, below) it is the same closed result a successful result is, its findings, follow_ups, covered and checked_head included (decision 0034 ruling 6, fix rounds 0109a1r3 and r4).

allOf.description: v5's tool-to-turn dependency, kept for every old-shaped and native observed row. Only a settled broker checkpoint, whose attempt and call identity give it ownership, may omit a turn no measured correlation supplied.
A retained response digest rides only beside a terminal outcome that has a response: never beside observed, refused or interrupted.
An unattributed tool keeps v5's 80-byte bound; only an attributed one may use the 256 bytes, and never by truncation.

A row this engine stamped that says it resumed carries the root it rejoined. Scoped on site_ref so no row another producer wrote — including every valid 0.10.0 row written before this contract — is newly refused.
A row this engine stamped names a refused offer only beside the cold launch that refusal produced. Scoped on site_ref for the same reason.

A row the engine authored beside a verdict carries its result closed. Scoped on authored, which only this contract's writer emits and v6's closed checkpoint refuses, so no row a v6-era engine wrote, the tagged 0.14.0 and 0.15.0 engines' included, is newly refused (fix round 0109a1r4).

result.description: A successful typed phase result plus the seat record reported beside it. result, inputs, notes and state are phase-machine/report fields, and findings, follow_ups and covered are decision 0109's separately governed gate report; none is permission for harness prose in accounting fields.

state.description: The dialect state command's output for this step, captured by the exec driver beside notes (decision 0042). Part of the separately governed typed report, like result, inputs and notes: this contract admits the field and governs none of its content. Absent on every record but a dialect step's, and on a dialect step whose dialect declares no state command.

findings.description: The seat's findings, each with the site the engine stamped (decision 0109 rulings 1 and 3). Absent and [] are the same empty set.

follow_ups.description: Non-blocking findings the engine carries (decision 0109 ruling 5): engine-written, and refused from a seat.

checked_head.description: The head the protected phase's effect's stable-head check accepted (decision 0109 ruling 7): engine-written, journaled with the result so decide records it as reviewed_heads from the journal and a resumed engine decides on the same head; refused from a seat.

sha256.description: 64 lowercase hex characters: a SHA-256 digest.

repo_path.description: A repository-relative path: non-empty, at most 4096 characters, never absolute, and with no '..' component, exactly what the engine's reader admits.

finding.description: One finding as the engine journals it (decision 0109 ruling 3): the seat's report, with the site the engine stamped. The key is (site, id).

site.description: The 64-hex digest of the compiled structural site that reported the finding, stamped by the engine; a seat never writes it.

id.description: The seat's stable identifier for the finding, the same across visits.

file.description: Where the finding is: a locator, not the identity.

line.description: A positive line locator, not the identity: an integer from 1 to the reader's bound, 2^64 - 1, written as an integer. The fence also reads every finding through the engine's typed reader, so a value this schema's integer admits that the reader does not, such as 1.0, is refused there; the two copies of this bound are the reader's and this one.

covered.description: What the verdict covered, engine-written (decision 0109 ruling 7). The head arm has two field sets, exactly one of head or head_digest, and records no base; the artifacts arm names each declared file and its SHA-256.

oneOf.description: A gate with its own head record: the commit it read.
The protected phase: the SHA-256 of the decide-time head string, a digest-pinned projection of reviewed_heads and never a third head authority.
A spec gate: each declared artifact file and its SHA-256, taken before the gate ran.
